newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Nokia falls on downgrade.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Nokia falls on downgrade.

text.p: American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) in Finnish mobile phone company Nokia Group fell on Tuesday with a ratings downgrade.
An ADR trader called the overall market "drifty" from a steady dollar.
"People are more cautious after we broke through the 7,000 (on the Dow Jones Industrial Average). Everything feels a little tired," he said.
Nokia fell 1-7/8 to 59-3/4 after NatWest Securities cut the company's rating to add from buy. Further details were not immediately available, and volume was almost 950,000 shares before midday.
ADRs in Chinese and Hong Kong stocks were largely unchanged in light volume despite rumors Chinese leader Deng Xiaaping's health was declining.
Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd was up 1/8 to 17-1/4 and Shandong Huaneng Power Development Co rose 3/8 to 10-1/2.
Jardine Fleming China Region Fund Inc was off 1/4 to 11-1/2 and Brilliance China Automotive Holdings Ltd was off 1/8 to 4-5/8.
"No one is really panicking," a trader said. "I don't think people in the United States are really concerned about the Deng Xiaoping thing."
ADRs in Spain's Telefonica de Espana SA were unchanged at 70-1/8 after the company's privatization.
Britain's Glaxo Wellcome Plc fell 1-1/8 to 32-3/4 on profit-taking and following comments from the company's chief executive that it would focus on small acquisitions.
Britain's Barclays Plc fell 8-1/2 to 71-1/2 after it reported 1996 pre-tax profits at the low end of expectations and a slump in its investment banking unit BZW.
Among Latin American ADRs, Brazilian telecommunications holding Telebras rose 1-1/2 to 95-3/4 in moderate volume.
Decliners led advancers by 294 to 241 among 807 ADRs. Volume at midday was 43 million shares.
